title: Why Is the Handle Far? Torque Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A long spanner loosens a stuck nut. A pedal turns on a long crank. A door opens at its handle. And when Aarav pushes a heavy college door near its hinges, it barely moves, but the same push at the handle swings it open. Why does the spot matter? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we learn torque, the turning effect of a force.

On a live motion notebook a door seen from above gets the same 20 N push at three distances while the readout tracks r, F, theta and the torque, and a graph shows torque growing in a straight line with distance. A slow-mo replay shows the position vector r and the push F, then a slanted push cuts the torque. We build the formula step by step (torque = r cross F, size r F sin theta, the moment arm r sin theta, unit newton metre, the right hand rule), see link by link why handles sit far from the hinge, compare a push at right angles with a slanted push, and solve a bicycle pedal example. Then the exam trap (distance to the point vs distance to the line of the force), an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
